players.product: LIDE laser-induced deep etching for glass-core substrates and through-glass vias (TGV)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Peter Mümmler: H1 2026 revenue was EUR 36.5 million, below last year mainly because Solar lacked a big order; adjusted EBIT was -EUR 10.4 million, cushioned by EUR 3 million-EUR 4 million of North Star fixed-cost savings, and free cash flow was -EUR 11.5 million, within expectations. Solar lost roughly EUR 18 million of revenue versus last year (about EUR 6 million profit impact) as the market waits for perovskites; Welding fell after last year's large Q1 consumer-electronics contract; Electronics grew slightly but stays loss-making as LPKF invests in LIDE; Development (rapid prototyping) declined on weak US public-sector demand, while CEO Klaus Fiedler cited demand above expectations from China and Europe and SMT laser depaneling saw investment restraint in Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue EUR 36.5 million; adjusted EBIT -EUR 10.4 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Peter Mümmler: orders on hand were EUR 34.7 million at the end of June, the same level as last year and a key element to keep stable in H2; CEO Klaus Fiedler: order entry grew slightly in H1. CFO: contract liabilities reflect down payments LPKF collects from customers.

CEO Klaus Fiedler: the 2026 guidance and the midterm aspiration are unchanged and achievable, with a much stronger second half as usual and a funnel holding more than sufficient opportunities; Solar is planned at less than half of its record 2024 revenue, and LPKF still anticipates one single-digit-million Solar deal from Asia in H2 revenue. LPKF targets a sustainable double-digit EBIT margin by 2028; CFO Peter Mümmler: after North Star the break-even will be below EUR 120 million of revenue.

CEO Klaus Fiedler: the dominating part of the players that have made an equipment decision for glass-based advanced packaging selected LPKF's LIDE, and the first of them have reached the process maturity to place ramp-up orders; negotiations are running now for ramp-ups in 2027, LPKF won one deal in Q1 and expects to report the first ramp-up deals won this year, aiming to win the majority (it cannot be a single-source market). Other players place ramp-up orders in 2027, and high-volume production is expected in 2029-2030 with deals distributed around 2028. Q2 LIDE orders were individual portfolio orders, not ramp-up orders: one large specialty glass company ordered one machine, with potential for more short term, and a university ordered too. LPKF now offers three process steps (LIDE, ABF / RDL ablation and glass-glass bonding), targets 70% of the 2030 glass market, and is defending its IP in a running lawsuit.

CEO Klaus Fiedler: a year ago LPKF estimated a 2030 total addressable market of about EUR 500 million for the equipment it can provide; the updated model, driven mainly by sharply higher projected high-performance-computing wafer starts and the broader portfolio, is very significantly larger. Management: co-packaged optics, using the glass core as the medium for dies to communicate optically, is in the R&D phase; LPKF goes into a positioning phase from 2027, expects no ramp-ups before 2029 and no high volume before 2030-2031, and has not included CPO in its TAM.
quarterly_data.figure: prior 2030 TAM estimate about EUR 500 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Klaus Fiedler: in LPKF's modeling its current capacity covers even the bull case for the next two years, and a decision on how and where to expand capacity must be taken within 2027. CFO Peter Mümmler: production is assembly-based, not capex-intensive, so the pace of adding capacity depends on hiring and training people.

CEO Klaus Fiedler: LPKF is positioned in perovskite solar with first prototyping lines in the USA and Asia and expects perovskite ramp-ups in 2028; if 20% of solar capacity added a perovskite tandem layer, the scribing-equipment market would reach a high nine-figure sum, versus LPKF's best Solar year of EUR 40 million. LPKF needs Solar volume orders that turn into revenue in 2027.
